title: Archimedes' principle and floating equilibrium practice

evidence_basis.originality_policy: Contexts, wording, values and diagram briefs are original; mapped evidence contributes assessment demand only.

question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions exercise prior learning: q01 directly retrieves Lesson 10 and q07 mixes Lesson 10 and Module 3 pressure knowledge with the current lesson.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: pressure-origin retrieval, three focused diagnostics, direct displaced-volume calculation, floating-density application, then mixed pressure and Archimedes reasoning

questions.prompt: A cuboid is completely submerged in a stationary liquid. Explain why the liquid exerts a resultant upward force on the cuboid.
A rigid object remains fully submerged in the same liquid and is moved to a greater depth. Which statement about its upthrust is correct?

options.A: It increases because the pressure is greater.
options.B: It decreases because the object is farther from the surface.
options.C: It stays constant because fluid density and displaced volume stay constant.
options.D: It becomes equal to the object's weight at every depth.

questions.prompt: The same wooden block floats first in water and then in a denser salt solution. What happens in the salt solution?

options.A: Its weight increases and it sinks farther.
options.B: It displaces a smaller volume because the same weight is supported by denser fluid.
options.C: It displaces the same volume because its own volume is unchanged.
options.D: Its upthrust becomes greater than its weight while it remains at rest.

questions.prompt: A uniform solid of density 650 kg m⁻³ floats freely in a liquid of density 1000 kg m⁻³. What percentage of the solid's volume is submerged?

questions.context: A rectangular inspection case of dimensions 0.40 m by 0.25 m by 0.18 m is held fully submerged in fresh water of density 1000 kg m⁻³. Its weight is 250 N. A vertical cable from above keeps it at rest. Use g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹.

figure.purpose: Assess force directions and displaced volume without giving the solution.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a rectangular case fully underwater, attached to a vertical cable from above. Label its three dimensions and show the water surface. Include no force arrows, equations or calculated values.
figure.alt_text: A rectangular case with labelled dimensions is fully submerged and held by a cable from above.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of water displaced by the case.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the upthrust on the case.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the cable and state its direction on the case.

questions.context: A vertical cylindrical float of mass 48 kg and constant cross-sectional area 0.20 m² floats freely in oil of density 800 kg m⁻³. Use g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State the two vertical forces on the float and the relationship between their magnitudes.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the volume of oil displaced.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the submerged depth of the float in the oil.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: The float is moved to water of density 1000 kg m⁻³. Calculate its new submerged depth and explain why it is smaller.

questions.context: A sealed block has horizontal top and bottom faces, each of area 0.060 m². The faces are 0.25 m apart vertically. The block is fully submerged in a stationary brine of density 1200 kg m⁻³ and is held at rest by a vertical cable from above. Its weight is 210 N. Use g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹.

figure.purpose: Assess the link from top and bottom pressure forces to Archimedes' principle and equilibrium.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a sealed rectangular block fully submerged in brine with horizontal top and bottom faces, vertical separation 0.25 m, face area 0.060 m squared and a cable from above. Label top and bottom faces but include no force arrows or equations.
figure.alt_text: A sealed block with labelled face area and height is fully submerged in brine and held by a cable.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Explain why the pressure forces on the block produce an upward resultant.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine how much greater the pressure is at the lower face than at the upper face.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use the pressure difference to calculate the upthrust. Check your result using Archimedes' principle.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the cable and state its direction on the block.
